unitTargets: ▸  I can describe a vector by its magnitude and direction, and resolve it into components.
▸  I can add vectors, at right angles and at any angle, and report the resultant with a direction.
▸  I can split a projectile’s motion into two axes that share one time.
▸  I can solve flat, angled and different-height launches using one shared time.
keyTerms: ▸  North of East, East of North
howItWorks: The left column names what to record. The open space beside it is for the board: write, sketch, label. Use as much of it as the slide needs.
Worked examples print the problem. Copy the setup and every step from the board, and carry units the whole way.
Your Turn: work it in the box first, then check against the board before the next slide.
Every vector answer carries a direction. Every number carries a unit.
Projectile problems: +y is up, so down is negative. Neglect air resistance.

sectionsContent.title: Vectors & Vector Basics (Review)
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can describe a vector by its magnitude and direction, name a direction two ways, and resolve a vector into x- and y-components.

cues: Length as magnitude, angle as direction

problem.statement: A hiker walks 50 m at 30° above the horizontal. Find the x- and y-components.

cues: The relationship between the two angles

problem.statement: A vector points 40° North of East. Express its direction as an angle East of North.

cues: Work it first, then check the board

problem.statement: A hiker walks at 65° East of North. Express this as an angle North of East.

cues: Work it first, then check the board

problem.statement: A force of 20 N acts at 70° East of North. Find its angle North of East, then resolve its components.

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: why is a number alone not enough to describe a vector, and what do you need to resolve one into components?
selfCheck: I can draw a vector and label its tail, tip and angle.
I can convert North of East to East of North.
I can resolve a vector into x- and y-components.

sectionsContent.title: Vector Addition
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can add two vectors, at 90° or at any angle, and state the resultant’s magnitude and direction.

cues: Common error — a magnitude with no direction

problem.statement: A plane flies 80 km/h east relative to the air. A wind blows 20 km/h north. Find the plane’s velocity relative to the ground.

cues: Add x to x and y to y
Extra digits kept until the final answer
rows.notesLabel: EXAMPLE — TWO FORCES ON A BOX

problem.statement: A 40 N force acts east, and a 30 N force acts 60° above east. Find the resultant force.

cues: Work it first, then check the board

problem.statement: Walk 30 m east, then 40 m at 45° above east. Find the resultant displacement.

cues: Work it first, then check the board
rows.notesLabel: PRACTICE — THREE FORCES ON A CRATE

problem.statement: Three ropes pull on a crate: 30 N east, 40 N north, and 20 N at 30° south of west. Find the resultant force.

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: when can you use the right-triangle shortcut, and what do you do when you cannot?
selfCheck: I can add two perpendicular vectors.
I can add vectors at any angle using components.
I can state a resultant with magnitude and direction.

sectionsContent.title: Projectile Motion (All Types)
sectionsContent.learningTarget: I can split a projectile’s motion into two axes, solve the vertical motion for time, and use that time horizontally.

cues: Horizontal velocity with no air resistance
Common error — a force is needed to keep it moving sideways
Vertical motion first, for the shared time

problem.statement: A ball rolls off a 0.80 m table at 2.5 m/s. How long until it lands, and how far does it travel horizontally?

cues: Work it first, then check the board
rows.notesLabel: YOUR TURN — OFF A HIGHER SHELF

problem.statement: A marble rolls off a 1.25 m shelf at 3.0 m/s. How far from the shelf does it land?

cues: Time of flight, and when it applies
Time depends on viy, range on both components

problem.statement: A ball is kicked at 18 m/s at 30° above level ground. Find its time of flight and range.

cues: Resolve first, then the level-ground formulas
Work it first, then check the board

problem.statement: An arrow is shot at 45 m/s at 40° above level ground. Find its range, neglecting air resistance.

cues: Height above launch, then above ground
rows.notesLabel: EXAMPLE — MAX HEIGHT FROM A CLIFF

problem.statement: A rock is launched at 20 m/s at 35° from a 15 m cliff. Find its maximum height above the launch point.

cues: The quadratic and the root to keep

problem.statement: The same rock (20 m/s, 35°, from a 15 m cliff) lands on the ground below. Find its total time of flight.

cues: The quantity shared by both axes

sectionsContent.summaryPrompt: In your own words: explain how one projectile moves with constant velocity in one direction and accelerates in the other, and what the two motions share.
selfCheck: I can find the time from the vertical motion and use it horizontally.
I can solve a flat, an angled and a different-height launch.
I can find the peak height and the total flight time from a cliff.

checklist: Your Turn problems checked against the board
close.bigPicture: Trace one projectile all the way through: resolve the launch velocity, solve the vertical motion for time, then use that same time horizontally.
